hypothesis: Cross-sectional momentum is stronger among relatively less-liquid but still tradable cryptocurrencies because limits to arbitrage slow correction of past-return signals.
universe: At each Monday 00:00 UTC, require exact prior daily history and rank eligible Binance USD-M USDT perpetuals by lagged trailing-30-day quote volume. Retain the top 100 for tradability, then define the relatively illiquid half as ranks 51-100. No future listing or return information enters eligibility.
feature: Lagged close-to-close momentum over W completed UTC days, ranked only within the relatively illiquid half of the top-100 liquidity universe.
portfolio: Equal-weight market-neutral long top momentum quintile and short bottom momentum quintile within the relatively illiquid half, 0.5 gross each side.
execution: All feature and liquidity inputs end Sunday; rebalance Monday open and hold to next Monday open.
development_gate: Canonical rank IC >0.02 with HAC p<0.05, positive winner-minus-loser spread, canonical net Sharpe >0.70 and total return >0, and at least 2/3 momentum windows positive after costs.
success_gate: Canonical OOS net Sharpe >1.0; OOS rank IC >0.02; positive at 2x costs; at least 2/3 windows positive; 2024 and 2025 each non-negative; max drawdown <35%; excluding BTC/ETH positive; excluding strongest contributor positive; DSR reported.
notes: This is a single pre-specified interaction, not a sweep across the paper's 40 characteristics. The top-100 then lower-half rule is fixed ex ante to balance limits-to-arbitrage exposure against tradability.
